title: Routing
description: How the router lays copper: how it searches, how a track a reader carries is held, and how a whole pcb is routed. Data, beside this class (#SECTION); what a reader chooses — the angle, walk or shove, jogs — comes with each request.

$schema.description: the schema this file is written to

routing.description: how a way is searched and shaped, whatever asks for it

searches.description: the searches tried one after another, quick and coarse first

items.description: One search over a grid: its step as a share of a track's width and gap, and how far round the two ends it looks, in steps.

share.description: the grid's step, as a share of half a track's width and gap together

margin.description: how far past the leg's two ends the grid reaches, in its own steps

turnCost.description: what a corner costs a way, in steps

searchLimit.description: the most grid points a search looks at, laying copper that has the time

shortestRun.description: a jog — a step shorter than this many track widths — goes from a line the router found

leastStep.description: a step shorter than this many track widths, which nobody can mean, goes from every line

worthShortening.description: how much shorter, in millimetres, a line has to come out to be laid again

shoveSampling.description: how often a track shoved aside is looked at along its length, in millimetres

fanOutReach.description: how far a neck out of a fine pitch may go, in millimetres

fanOutStep.description: how finely a neck's end is looked for, in millimetres

neckShares.description: how thin a neck may be, as shares of the track's width, the widest first; 0 is the rules' least

stopHalvings.description: how many halvings find where a track stops short of what it cannot pass

bucket.description: how wide a cell of a fence's index is, in millimetres: a few tracks' worth

roomLooked.description: how far round a point its room is looked for, in millimetres: a few steps of the finest search

carrying.description: how a track a reader drags is held to the pointer

searchLimit.description: the most grid points a search looks at while a reader drags: it has a frame to answer in

holdSteps.description: how many halvings find how far a drag can go where it cannot go all the way

bandStep.description: how finely the point a track is pulled by moves towards the pointer, in millimetres

frameBudget.description: how long the tracks a moved part pulls are searched for, a frame at a time, in milliseconds

endStub.description: how far a corner carried stands out before the line goes on, in millimetres

widestDetour.description: how much longer than straight a line going on from a carried corner may be

longestWalk.description: how much longer than the line asked for a walk round what is in the way may come out

autorouting.description: how a whole pcb's connections are laid

angleStep.description: the directions an autorouted track may take where the reader does not lay at right angles

viaOffEnds.description: how far off the two ends of a connection a via stands at least, in millimetres

attempts.description: the most connections tried in a round

decimals.description: the places a laid point is written to

layerDirections.description: the way each outer layer's tracks run, so the layers cross rather than fight for the same channels

innerDirections.description: the ways inner layers' tracks run, one after another

againstDirection.description: what a step across a layer's way costs, as a share of a step along it

budgetSeconds.description: how long a routing runs at most

planeDrops.description: Pads dropped onto their plane: how far out of the pad the via may stand, and how finely it is looked for, in millimetres.

reach.description: how far out of its pad a drop's via may stand, in millimetres

step.description: how finely the via's place is looked for, in millimetres

ripUp.description: how a refused connection is retried by lifting what was laid

passes.description: how many times the refused are retried by lifting what was laid

candidates.description: how many routes near a refused connection are lifted one at a time

margin.description: how far round a connection's box a route stands near it, in millimetres

rounds.description: how many rounds a routing has, each giving the refused the room first

viaCost.description: what changing layer costs, in steps

link.description: A 0 Ω link over what is in the way: the footprint it stands on, the letters its designator starts with, and what it costs in steps.

footprint.description: the footprint a 0 Ω link stands on, by slug

designator.description: the letters a link is named with, before its number

cost.description: what a link costs a way, in grid steps: dearer than a via, so it is laid only where nothing else goes

tuning.description: how a track is bent to a length

amplitude.description: a meander's tallest bump, in millimetres

spacing.description: how far apart its sides stand, in track widths — never nearer than a track and its gap

tolerance.description: how near a length is brought, in millimetres: well inside any skew a pair allows

bumpsTried.description: how many more bumps are tried, past the fewest the tallest bump allows, before a segment is too short
